headline: Business Insider found that business leaders including Jeff Bezos and Jamie Dimon are predicting AI will shorten the working week to about three days.
score_reason: Pool score kept: feature summarising leaders' predictions with a fresh expert view; predictions, not outcomes.
importance_line: Workers are the people affected, yet the predictions come from executives whose firms profit from AI, and none of them is a plan or a promise of pay for a shorter week.
summary: Business Insider reports that Jeff Bezos, founder and chairman of Amazon, told Fox News last week that AI will let people do in three days what took five, and that Jamie Dimon, chief executive of JPMorgan Chase, Zoom chief executive Eric Yuan and Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates have made similar predictions, while Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, says "we never get the promise of the four-hour workweek at mass scale in society." Alex Tabarrok, an economics professor at George Mason University, told the outlet a shorter week is more likely than mass unemployment, and wrote in an April blog post that the difference between catastrophe and wonderland "boils down to distribution".
notes: A roundup of statements made over months; Bezos's remark was 'last week'. Kept at 5 because the compilation and Tabarrok's comment are from this week.
